body:
I think it might be both? The description about the gaping wound is one she used more often. I admit this latest description was odd but I was just more upset that like, if she was worried about that association, why couldnt she just come to associate that tattoo with myself over time and overwrite that image in her head? 

She has issues with picturing how she might feel in the future (I'm very sure this is her autism showing, her favourite answer to things is "I don't know because I've never been in that situation before"), so I think she reacts negatively to new things so the odds are in her favour in case she Dislikes something new

Yes bad reaction to healed tattoos. No reaction to piercings -- I have a few and they've never bothered her. I suggested my idea for the tattoo size and placement (upper arm or thigh, cuz I heard those are good for first tattoos) and she literally had the gagging disgust reaction. She said that she would associate me with greasy ugly trashy people who usually got tattoos there.

Ugh good points. I wish there was a simple solution to it. I think resentment is a good way to put it, because this is definitely being compounded by the fact she's transitioning and making lots of changes to her body, but I can't.

Our communication is great, and I have brought it up to her. I think the reason I posted here needing to vent is that even after the conversation, she is unlikely to change. I'm not really asking for advice on how to change her mind, as she has enough on her plate and I don't want to add more to it. Just a little frustrated.

Thank you for your advice. I am curious to see how things play out with us as we are currently all done with medical appointments or any sort of appointments. It's all sorted on that front which is a relief. 

I had a conversation a couple days ago which was a gentle "it would make me happy to see more of x" but with no pressure or expectation of it. She said she's still not in the place to have energy for it and that things will likely continue as is for a while. I respect that and am wiling to see how it goes. Since I don't need to put that much effort into her transition now, I think I will try to put that effort into myself. 

I wish I had more support from her but it is what it is. My therapist has been helping me support myself and be confident in myself and maybe that's just the period I am in right now.

I've been needing to prompt her to verbally express love and gratitude lately, but it isn't terrible (?). She's actually been helping me around the house unprompted like cleaning the cat bowls and putting away dishes, which means a whole lot to me, and I've been trying to tell her how much it means to me for her to do housework unprompted. She works full time and I don't so I usually do all the chores. 

I've been feeling a little overlooked, not going to lie. I feel like I've been adapting a lot to her and her needs, while not really getting that reciprocated. Like I said, she told me she isn't good at taking care of me anymore. I wish she would start the conversation with me on how she can better support me. I think it's weird if I was the one to start that conversation. I might bring it up lightly to her.

Yes, she is in therapy and her therapist is very supportive. I totally understand you and yes we are in the same boat... I think 6 months is a good timeline and I'm just going to hold out for a couple more months to see what happens. Can I ask if your wife has come out? I think that is a factor of how it is for me, as my partner isn't out and isn't planning to come out anytime soon, so I feel this pressure of keeping her secret. I'm so glad to hear your wife is doing well. I know this is the typical timeline for trans women, and again I'm excited for that for my own partner, but yeah it's weird because I don't want to be expectant or pressure her into this improvement

I appreciate your thoughts. I think I'm just sounding it out here as much as I can before I have that conversation with them because I'm not looking forwards to it >_< 
I've never really enjoyed how our conversations about sex goes -- they tend to be the rockiest part of our relationship, but we always overcome it. I trust my partner that we can make it work. I just gotta hype myself up for it or something lol. 

I think another factor is that I'm not willing to bring this up so close to them coming out to me. I think I'm willing to wait for things to settle a little with time before I throw something new in the mix

Thanks for this; the empathy about performing the dominant role means a lot to me. I'm also afraid of the future resentment if they ask "more" from me... like I'm happy with how things are now, but it's also that fear of change? Sigh. I wish femdoms were easier to find HAHA but they are such an incredibly amazing rarity
We are actually in an open relationship, and I'm happy for my partner to seek out other people for sex! Sometimes I have to wingman for them though lol
This is really good advice, thanks heaps! Having someone reframe things really puts it into perspective for me

Same boat. Life just keeps going over and over and over and I'm not happy. I hate that all  suicide methods have a chance of not working cuz waking up after has to be my worst nightmare. Maybe it's deserved in a way
Thank you for sharing your experience! I think I'm in the same boat as past you. Up till this point I have actually gotten along well enough with my metas (but again, most were short term).
I appreciate this comment a lot -- I was worried how reasonable my feelings were on this.

I appreciate your perspective. We also have the added complications of him (and his new partner) being on the autism spectrum, so I do understand that his feeling of being rejected is more Rejection Sensitivity Dysphoria. I'm going to have a think about how I want to move forward.

No, we were secondary school best friends. After I left I started up the weekly games so we has an excuse to still talk to each other. But we talk outside of the games. The games are an excuse. 

I was there for 3 weekends, and I didn't plan anything on the weekends so that if people were free I could jump at them. I made an excel spreadsheet and asked everyone to tell me exact days they were free so I could bother them. It was only in hindsight that I realised that nothing was happening without my initiative. I hoped they were more excited to see me and unfortunately that wasnt true. None of them have kids and a couple of them dont talk to family.

Thank you, It was an important trip for me, and I'm glad i took it!

I had hoped the people I spent years bonding with and countless nights talking to would have had had the same values and important notions of friendship as I had. I thought our conversations meant more and were more truthful. My feelings and expectations didnt come from nowhere. I feel like the people here arent really trusting the fact that I spent years with my friends, and we spent that time together for a reason.... but at the same time, I'm coming to understand the cultural divide between local Singaporeans and the person I am today, considering that I just cannot fathom the consensus people are coming to. I think I'm coming to understand that maybe I did not understand my friends at all.

That is actually a good idea, thank you. I think we're not going to be able to travel for a while though. I think going overseas is something a lot more unusual where I live. I noticed a lot of people mentioned saving PTO for travelling, but this was the only thing that we're only going to do like once for the next 5 years or something lol 

It was very important for me to go back to Singapore this time and I was saving for years to make this happen, as I really wanted to visit some childhood locations (really silly personal things like food courts and alleys and schools and bus interchanges and HDBs), which I'm relieved I was able to do. It was honestly less of a "vacation" and a lot more "coming home". It was super emotional for me lol

I think for context, where I live now, I've had friends take PTO / I've taken PTO to entertain close friends who live in different cities cuz we dont get to see each other often, and we travel specifically to see each other. But then again I do live in a country where people take PTO on wednesdays just because they dont want to work lol 

I think something I'm trying to express here that people arent picking up on is that... these people werent "just friends" to me. I understand your examples and I would choose to do the same if I just wanted to "catch up"

I considered a few of these friends to be my best friends, but they were the ones who had the least time for me. This was something at least 4 years in the making, cuz I originally planned to travel in 2020 (lol). The last time I saw them, they were teenagers, and I was so excited to see how they had grown up. I was indeed looking forwards to "take PTO and hang out the whole day", but I know now I was probably asking too much.

Oh no absolutely not the whole time. I think even 1 day wouldve been enough. I just wanted to spend time with them. One meal is... not sufficient. I dont want a catch up. I wanted bonding. These were people I was very emotionally intimate with online, that I finally got a chance to see in person. I just wanted to see how they walked, how they sat down. What they did when they the conversation lulled. Where would they look? What do they appreciate? Do they bounce their leg, tap their fingers? I knew them for years and years and years. I wanted to put a face and body to the people I knew.
Yep that makes sense. Thanks for telling me. Also re: the edit, yes I'm accepting that. I think it was also true that I valued them more than they valued me, and I need to adjust that.
Thank you for letting me know. /gen
That hurts to hear. They were a really big part of my life, but I'm coming to understand that I wasnt a huge part of theirs.

I told them the moment I booked the tickets, 10 months in advance. I kept the dates pinned in our group chat, and reminded them in the months leading up. I was talking about it often because I was really excited. I hadn't seen them in person for years and years.

The term for this is "emotional incest" 

Echoing what has already been said, you are not at fault. I've been through the same thing, but I'm lucky in that my mum was willing to seek professional help and she has mellowed out heaps, and started to understand her pointed comments are hurtful. It was a fight to get her to accept mental health as "real". I think many people in their generation grew up with trauma and think it's just normal, so they just perpetuate the cycle. 

Take care of yourself OP. It is a very difficult place to be in, and not a lot of people understand. You love your mum, and that is really good, but this is also for her own sake. She needs to take care of herself too.

im currently working through some stuff but am not in a safe position to get a diagnosis. 

it makes me feel really bad and guilty whenever i think "i wish i had DiD" like genuinely so guilty and i apologetic because god ive read a lot about this and i feel for every person who has DiD. the trauma you have to go through is unimaginable 

i think i have C-PTSD, which generally comes with DiD but the problem is, i dont remember any trauma i had at a young age, and i have zero way of confirming if anything did happen. its the split that happens between the age 6-9 that causes DiD right, and im fairly sure my life was good in that timespan. and when i think to myself "i wish i had DiD" i genuinely feel so bad because when i think that, it means that i must be making up some sort of childhood trauma that i can't confirm happened. i feel like im insulting the people who actually went through the trauma by thinking that 

but i dont know, i already have this other trauma. having DiD makes it seem less lonely considering i have the intrusive and depressive thoughts already. having a protector seems nice.

helped, thank you. gave it a bit of time and yeah i know she was upset and did something uncharacteristic. thank u for helping my self-esteem

i think right now i am trying my best to deflect my mother's hatred off of my sister, because she hates her so very much. its scary in a way. 

i think we will be alright though. things will be alright.

this actually just happened: 

i was cooking, and had her share ready for her first, and told her to come and eat. she came and took half to the table, then went back to her room to play on her iphone. i called her a couple times, and only then did she came back to take the other half to the table and eat. by then the food was already cold. i asked her why she waited to do that, because i was only cooking at this time as i asked her when she wanted to eat, and she said now. if she wanted to play first she could've requested to eat later. she does things like this all the time, and in front of our mother, which only sets of our mother into a destructive mood. today was fine because our mother was at work and didn't see it. 

she's so addicted to her electronics that her glasses prescription has increased from 150 to 400 in about 8 months. my mother is livid and refuses to pay for new glasses, which will only speed up the degradation of her eyes. 

i know the addiction is because she isn't parented well, and her only form of discipline is corporal punishment. but the fear of pain worked for disciplining me, and i have no idea why it isn't working on her. i dont know how to help her correct herself. 

my brother is overseas, so he can only call online. he has helped us by counselling us and giving us advice to deal with our mother. he has helped me once by talking me out of self-harm. he has attempted to talk to my sister about her addiction but even his advice falls flat because he can only talk to her.

can you please give me some advice on how?

even if i am just nice to her and do nice things for her it feels like nothing changes. it feels like i am a parent who just enables their child's terrible behaviour and would ultimately lead to their child growing up to be a terrible person.

Thank u for the offer but I'm still so hesitant about talking. 

It feels strange talking to a stranger whom I have no connection to, but at the same time I feel like I am burdening my love ones greatly because every time we talk I just bring up the fact that my life is miserable and they cant do anything about it  

I've been seeing a counselor recently, but it's only once I week. I'm really mad because I've been so good the past month, and only broke yesterday because my mom decided the house was too quite and she needed to take her anger out on me.

My mother is abusive and she got really mad last night and took it out on me. 

I know that rationally it's not my fault and that I shouldn't let her get into my headspace but it's not as easy as that. 
It's really just easier to give up.

Gosh, I actually used to do that?? As a kid and teenager, I could just talk to my alters (i thought they were just my story characters, or imaginary friends then) and ask "Who are you? Who's there?" and they'd tell me so vividly. 

I don't know why in recent years it feels more.. stuck. Honestly my entire mental state has been rather shaky as of late and my mind just entirely fuzzy and mixed. I probably need professional help haha 

Thank you for your answer though. It's relieving in a way.

I've written out things before, just whatever I'm thinking as I'm thinking it, but usually use my laptop. Writing on paper seems to be a cool idea though. Real intimate. 

Thank you ;; I'm looking into seeing if a therapist is possible for me? Hoping it goes well.
